category: Layers, masks, smart objects and layer styles
description: Everything in the Layer menu and the Layers panel: creating and organising layers and groups, the four kinds of mask, smart objects and smart filters, the ten layer effects, blend modes and blending options, and the merge, align and blend commands.

tools.name: Layers panel
tools.description: The central control surface of a Photoshop document: the stacking order, visibility, opacity, fill, blend mode, locks, masks, effects, groups and colour labels of every layer. The filter bar at the top narrows the list by kind, name, effect, mode, attribute, colour or smart object. Most layer commands are also reachable from the panel's footer buttons and its context menus.
tools.usage: Window > Layers (F7).
tools.example:
1. Press F7 to show the panel.
2. Alt+click a layer's eye icon to solo it.
3. Ctrl+click layer thumbnails to select several, then Ctrl+G to group them.

tools.name: New Layer
tools.description: Adds an empty transparent layer above the active one. Holding Alt while clicking the panel's New Layer button (or using the menu command) opens a dialog for the name, colour label, blend mode, opacity, a clipping-mask option and the "Fill with neutral color" option used for non-destructive dodge-and-burn layers.
tools.usage: Layer > New > Layer... (Shift+Ctrl+N), or the New Layer button in the Layers panel (Ctrl+click adds it below the active layer).

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Blend mode of the new layer; Soft Light/Overlay unlock the neutral-colour option.

parameters.name: Fill with <mode>-neutral color
parameters.description: Fills with 50% grey (or black/white) so the layer is invisible until painted on.

parameters.name: Use Previous Layer to Create Clipping Mask
parameters.description: Clips the new layer to the one below.

tools.name: Layer via Copy / Layer via Cut
tools.description: Turns the current selection into a new layer, either copying the pixels (Ctrl+J) or cutting them out of the source layer (Shift+Ctrl+J). Ctrl+J with no selection duplicates the whole layer, which is the fastest way to start a non-destructive edit.
tools.usage: Layer > New > Layer via Copy (Ctrl+J) / Layer via Cut (Shift+Ctrl+J).
tools.example:
1. Select the subject with the Object Selection tool.
2. Ctrl+J to lift it onto its own layer.
3. Hide the original layer to check the cut-out against a coloured background.

tools.name: Duplicate Layer
tools.description: Copies a layer, group or smart object, optionally into another open document or a brand-new document. Duplicating into another document is the scripted way to composite files without copy-paste and without losing layer properties.
tools.usage: Layer > Duplicate Layer..., or right-click the layer in the Layers panel > Duplicate Layer. Ctrl+J duplicates in place.

parameters.name: As
parameters.description: Name for the duplicate.

parameters.name: Document
parameters.description: Target document, or New to create one.

tools.name: Delete Layer / Delete Hidden Layers
tools.description: Removes the selected layers, or in one command every layer whose visibility is off - a quick way to clean a working file before delivery. Deleting a group offers the choice of deleting the group and its contents or only the group.
tools.usage: Layer > Delete > Layer / Hidden Layers, the Delete key with the Move tool active, or the bin icon in the Layers panel (Alt+click skips the confirmation).

tools.name: Layer Groups
tools.description: Folders that hold layers, nest up to ten levels deep and can carry their own mask, opacity and blend mode - a group set to a mode other than Pass Through composites its contents first, then blends the result. Essential for organising composites and for masking many layers at once.
tools.usage: Layer > Group Layers (Ctrl+G), Layer > Ungroup Layers (Shift+Ctrl+G). Layer > New > Group from Layers... names it as it is created.
tools.example:
1. Select the sky replacement layers in the Layers panel.
2. Ctrl+G and name the group "sky".
3. Add a mask to the group - it now masks every layer inside.
tools.notes: Set the group's blend mode away from Pass Through when adjustment layers inside it should affect only the group.

tools.name: Arrange (layer stacking order)
tools.description: Moves layers up and down the stack: Bring to Front, Bring Forward, Send Backward, Send to Back, plus Reverse for several selected layers. Stacking order decides what covers what and which layers an adjustment layer or clipping mask affects.
tools.usage: Layer > Arrange > Bring to Front (Shift+Ctrl+]) / Bring Forward (Ctrl+]) / Send Backward (Ctrl+[) / Send to Back (Shift+Ctrl+[).
tools.example:
Select the logo layer and press Shift+Ctrl+] to place it above everything else.

JSX: layer.move(app.activeDocument.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEBEFORE);

tools.name: Layer Mask
tools.description: An 8-bit greyscale channel attached to a layer: white reveals, black hides, grey is partial transparency. The foundation of all non-destructive compositing - paint, gradient, filter or load a selection into the mask instead of erasing pixels. The Properties panel adds Density, Feather and a Select and Mask button for the active mask.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Mask > Reveal All / Hide All / Reveal Selection / Hide Selection, or the Add Layer Mask button in the Layers panel (Alt+click hides instead of reveals).

parameters.name: Density
parameters.description: Reduces the strength of the whole mask without repainting it.

parameters.name: Feather
parameters.description: Live, re-editable softening of the mask edge.

parameters.name: Invert
parameters.description: Ctrl+I with the mask selected swaps hidden and revealed areas.

tools.example:
1. Make a selection of the subject.
2. Click the Add Layer Mask button - the background is hidden.
3. Press B and paint with black/white on the mask to refine it. Alt+click the mask thumbnail to view the mask alone; Shift+click to disable it.
tools.notes: Ctrl+click a mask thumbnail loads it as a selection. Masks can be moved to another layer by dragging the thumbnail.

tools.name: Vector Mask
tools.description: Masks a layer with a resolution-independent path rather than pixels, giving permanently crisp edges that scale without softening. Ideal for UI elements, hard-edged product cut-outs and shapes that must stay razor sharp; combine with a pixel mask on the same layer when you need both hard and soft edges.
tools.usage: Layer > Vector Mask > Reveal All / Hide All / Current Path. Ctrl+click the Add Layer Mask button to add a vector mask to a layer that already has a pixel mask.
tools.example:
1. Draw a path around the object with the Pen tool.
2. Layer > Vector Mask > Current Path.
3. Edit the mask later with the Direct Selection tool (A) - the edge stays perfectly sharp at any zoom.
tools.notes: Layer > Rasterize > Vector Mask converts it to a pixel mask when you need to paint on it.

tools.name: Clipping Mask
tools.description: Confines a layer to the opaque pixels of the layer directly beneath it, shown by an indented thumbnail and a downward arrow. Used to keep an adjustment, a texture or a photo inside a shape, a type layer or a retouched subject without duplicating its mask.
tools.usage: Layer > Create Clipping Mask (Alt+Ctrl+G), or Alt+click the dividing line between two layers in the Layers panel.
tools.example:
1. Put a photo layer directly above a type layer.
2. Alt+Ctrl+G - the photo now shows only inside the letters.
3. Move the photo layer with the Move tool to reposition it within the type.
tools.notes: Several layers can clip to the same base layer. The base layer's blend mode governs the whole clipped stack.

tools.name: Disable, Apply and Delete Layer Mask
tools.description: Mask housekeeping: temporarily switch a mask off to compare, permanently bake the mask into the pixels, or throw the mask away and keep the full layer. Applying a mask is destructive and is normally only done to reduce file size on a finished file.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Mask > Disable / Enable / Apply / Delete. Shift+click the mask thumbnail toggles it; right-click the thumbnail for the same commands.
tools.example:
1. Shift+click the mask thumbnail - a red X appears and the whole layer shows.
2. Shift+click again to re-enable it.
3. Right-click > Apply Layer Mask only when you are certain the mask is final.
tools.notes: Apply Layer Mask is unavailable on smart objects and shape layers.

tools.name: Convert to Smart Object
tools.description: Wraps one or more layers in a container that preserves their original data, so transforms, warps and filters applied to it are re-editable and non-destructive. Scaling a smart object down and back up loses no quality, and its contents are edited in a separate document window.
tools.usage: Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object, or right-click the layer(s) in the Layers panel > Convert to Smart Object.
tools.example:
1. Select the four layers that make up the badge.
2. Right-click > Convert to Smart Object.
3. Ctrl+T and scale to 30% - the original resolution is retained inside.

JSX (Action Manager):
executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("newPlacedLayer"), undefined, DialogModes.NO);
tools.notes: Painting and cloning tools cannot be used directly on a smart object; double-click its thumbnail to edit the contents instead.

tools.name: Place Embedded / Place Linked
tools.description: Imports another file (PSD, AI, PDF, JPEG, raw) as a smart object. Place Embedded copies the data into the document; Place Linked keeps a reference to the file on disk so updating the source updates every document that links to it - the basis of template-driven production.
tools.usage: File > Place Embedded... / File > Place Linked... Commit the placement with Enter.

parameters.name: Linked file status
parameters.description: A link badge in the Layers panel shows out-of-date or missing links; Layer > Smart Objects > Update Modified Content / Relink to File resolves them.

parameters.name: Package
parameters.description: File > Package collects every linked file next to the PSD for hand-off.

tools.example:
1. File > Place Linked..., choose logo.ai, press Enter.
2. Edit logo.ai in Illustrator and save.
3. Back in Photoshop the layer shows an out-of-date badge; Layer > Smart Objects > Update Modified Content refreshes it.

tools.name: Edit Contents / Replace Contents (smart object)
tools.description: Opens a smart object's source in its own window (PSB for layered content, Illustrator for vector art, Camera Raw for a raw file) so it can be edited and saved back into the parent document, or swaps the source for a different file while keeping every transform, mask and effect already applied. Replace Contents is what makes a mockup template reusable.
tools.usage: Layer > Smart Objects > Edit Contents (or double-click the layer thumbnail) / Replace Contents...
tools.example:
1. Double-click the smart object thumbnail - it opens as a .psb.
2. Change the headline text and press Ctrl+S, then close the .psb.
3. The parent document updates automatically.
4. For a new product shot, use Layer > Smart Objects > Replace Contents and pick the new image.

tools.name: Smart Filters
tools.description: Any filter applied to a smart object is recorded as a re-editable smart filter with its own blending options, a shared filter mask and an eye icon. Double-click the filter name to change its settings, double-click the sliders icon to change its opacity and blend mode, and paint on the filter mask to limit where it applies.
tools.usage: Convert the layer to a smart object, then apply any filter. Layer > Smart Filters > Disable/Enable, Delete Filter Mask, Clear Smart Filters.
tools.example:
1. Convert the layer to a smart object (Filter > Convert for Smart Filters does it in one step).
2. Filter > Blur > Gaussian Blur, 8 px.
3. Select the white filter mask and paint with black over the subject so only the background stays blurred.
tools.notes: Filter Gallery, Liquify and Camera Raw Filter all work as smart filters; a handful of legacy filters do not.

tools.name: Drop Shadow (layer effect)
tools.description: Casts a shadow behind the layer's opaque pixels, offset by distance and angle and softened by size and spread. The most used layer effect for lifting UI elements, type and cut-outs off a background. Layer > Layer Style > Create Layer converts it into an editable pixel layer.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Drop Shadow..., or double-click the layer in the Layers panel to open Blending Options, or click the fx button in the panel footer.

parameters.name: Blend Mode / Color / Opacity
parameters.description: Usually Multiply with a dark colour sampled from the scene.

parameters.name: Angle / Use Global Light
parameters.description: Shadow direction; Global Light keeps every effect in the document consistent.

parameters.name: Distance / Spread / Size
parameters.description: Offset, how much of the blur is solid, and the blur radius.

parameters.name: Layer Knocks Out Drop Shadow
parameters.description: Prevents the shadow showing through a semi-transparent layer.

tools.example: Double-click the button layer, tick Drop Shadow, set Multiply / 30% / 90 degrees / Distance 2 px / Size 6 px.

tools.name: Inner Shadow (layer effect)
tools.description: Draws a shadow just inside the layer's edges, making the content look recessed or punched into the surface. Combined with a subtle Inner Glow it produces the classic inset field or engraved-type look.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Inner Shadow...

parameters.name: Distance / Choke / Size
parameters.description: Offset, hardness and blur of the interior shadow.

parameters.name: Angle / Use Global Light
parameters.description: Direction of the light source.

tools.example: Double-click a text input rectangle, tick Inner Shadow, Multiply 20%, Distance 1 px, Size 3 px to give it an inset look.

tools.name: Outer Glow (layer effect)
tools.description: Adds a soft halo of colour or gradient around the outside of the layer's pixels. Used for neon and light effects, for separating a subject from a busy background, and for focus rings in interface design.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Outer Glow...

parameters.name: Technique
parameters.description: Softer (smoothly blurred) or Precise (follows the shape tightly).

parameters.name: Spread / Size
parameters.description: How much of the glow is solid, and its overall radius.

parameters.name: Range / Jitter
parameters.description: Shape and randomisation of the glow's contour, mainly for gradient glows.

tools.example: Double-click a neon type layer, tick Outer Glow, Screen mode, a saturated cyan, Size 24 px, Spread 8%.

tools.name: Inner Glow (layer effect)
tools.description: Glows inwards from the layer's edges, or outwards from its centre when Source is set to Center. Useful for simulating rim light on a cut-out, adding a soft vignette inside a shape, or giving type a subtle inner light.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Inner Glow...

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: Edge (glow from the outline inwards) or Center (glow from the middle outwards).

parameters.name: Choke / Size
parameters.description: Hardness and radius of the glow.

tools.example: Double-click the layer, tick Inner Glow, Source = Edge, Screen 40%, Size 12 px.

tools.name: Bevel & Emboss (layer effect)
tools.description: Simulates a three-dimensional edge with highlight and shadow, with optional Contour and Texture sub-effects. Styles range from Outer/Inner Bevel and Emboss to Pillow Emboss and Stroke Emboss; Gloss Contour shapes the specular falloff.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Bevel & Emboss... (with the nested Contour and Texture checkboxes in the left-hand list).

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Outer Bevel, Inner Bevel, Emboss, Pillow Emboss, Stroke Emboss.

parameters.name: Technique
parameters.description: Smooth, Chisel Hard, Chisel Soft.

parameters.name: Depth / Size / Soften
parameters.description: Strength, extent and smoothing of the bevel.

parameters.name: Contour / Texture
parameters.description: Curve of the bevel profile; a pattern used as a bump map.

tools.example: Double-click a metal badge layer, tick Bevel & Emboss, Style = Inner Bevel, Technique = Chisel Hard, Depth 200%, Size 8 px, and add a Gloss Contour of "Ring - Double".

tools.name: Satin (layer effect)
tools.description: Applies an interior shading based on the layer's own shape, offset and inverted, producing a soft wavy sheen. Used for silky fabric, glass, chrome type and other reflective surface treatments.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Satin...

parameters.name: Angle / Distance / Size
parameters.description: Direction and scale of the offset copy that produces the sheen.

parameters.name: Contour / Invert
parameters.description: Shape of the falloff and whether the sheen is positive or negative.

tools.example: Double-click a chrome type layer, tick Satin, Multiply 30%, Angle 19 degrees, Distance 11 px, Size 14 px, Contour = Gaussian, Invert on.

tools.name: Color Overlay (layer effect)
tools.description: Floods the layer's opaque pixels with a single colour at a chosen blend mode and opacity, non-destructively. The quickest way to recolour an icon, a shape or type, and to build multi-state UI components without duplicating artwork.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Color Overlay...
tools.example:
1. Double-click the icon layer, tick Color Overlay.
2. Set the colour to the brand blue, Normal, 100%.
3. Alt+drag the fx badge onto another icon layer to copy the effect.

tools.name: Gradient Overlay (layer effect)
tools.description: Fills the layer with a gradient that can be linear, radial, angle, reflected or diamond, re-editable at any time and draggable on canvas while the dialog is open. Used for buttons, sky washes, metallic type and duotone treatments.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Gradient Overlay...

parameters.name: Gradient / Reverse
parameters.description: Choose or edit the gradient preset; reverse its direction.

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Linear, Radial, Angle, Reflected, Diamond.

parameters.name: Angle / Scale / Align with Layer
parameters.description: Direction, size and whether the gradient maps to the layer bounds.

parameters.name: Dither
parameters.description: Reduces banding in smooth gradients.

tools.example: Double-click the button layer, tick Gradient Overlay, pick a light-to-dark blue, Style = Linear, Angle 90 degrees, then drag on the canvas to reposition it.

tools.name: Pattern Overlay (layer effect)
tools.description: Tiles a pattern preset across the layer's opaque pixels at an adjustable scale and blend mode, and can be repositioned by dragging on the canvas. Used for fabric, paper, noise and halftone textures on type and shapes.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Pattern Overlay...

parameters.name: Pattern / Scale
parameters.description: Preset from the Patterns panel and its tiling size.

parameters.name: Link with Layer
parameters.description: Keeps the pattern registered to the layer when it is moved.

parameters.name: Snap to Origin
parameters.description: Resets the pattern offset to the document origin.

tools.example: Double-click a type layer, tick Pattern Overlay, choose a paper texture, Scale 50%, blend mode Multiply, opacity 30%.

tools.name: Stroke (layer effect)
tools.description: Outlines the layer's edges with a colour, gradient or pattern, positioned inside, outside or centred on the boundary. Non-destructive and resolution-independent, unlike Edit > Stroke which paints pixels.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Stroke...

parameters.name: Size / Position
parameters.description: Width in pixels; Outside, Inside or Center.

parameters.name: Fill Type
parameters.description: Color, Gradient or Pattern.

parameters.name: Blend Mode / Opacity
parameters.description: How the stroke composites with the layer.

tools.example: Double-click the cut-out layer, tick Stroke, Size 3 px, Position = Inside, white, to create a sticker outline.
tools.notes: Position = Inside keeps corners sharp on type; Outside rounds them.

tools.name: Blending Options and Blend If
tools.description: The top pane of the Layer Style dialog: general blending (mode and opacity), advanced blending (Fill Opacity, channel knockouts, Knockout, Blend Interior Effects as Group, Transparency Shapes Layer) and the Blend If sliders, which hide or reveal pixels of this layer or the underlying composite by luminance or channel value. Alt+drag a Blend If slider handle to split it for a smooth transition - the classic way to drop a sky or a texture into an image without a mask.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Blending Options..., or double-click an empty part of the layer row in the Layers panel.

parameters.name: Fill Opacity
parameters.description: Reduces the layer's pixels while leaving its layer effects at full strength.

parameters.name: Knockout
parameters.description: None, Shallow or Deep - punches through to the layer below or to transparency.

parameters.name: Blend If: This Layer
parameters.description: Hides pixels of the current layer by brightness range.

parameters.name: Blend If: Underlying Layer
parameters.description: Reveals the layer only where the composite below falls in a brightness range.

tools.example:
1. Put a texture layer above a photo and double-click it.
2. In Blend If: Underlying Layer, drag the white handle to 200 so the texture disappears from the highlights.
3. Alt+drag that handle apart (170 / 200) to feather the transition.

tools.name: Copy, Paste, Clear and Scale Layer Effects
tools.description: Reuses a built layer style across the document: copy the effect stack from one layer and paste it onto one or many others, clear it, or scale every distance, size and spread value at once so a style built at one size still looks right at another.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Copy Layer Style / Paste Layer Style / Clear Layer Style / Scale Effects..., or Alt+drag the fx badge between layers in the Layers panel (drag without Alt to move it).
tools.example:
1. Right-click the styled layer > Copy Layer Style.
2. Select the other five buttons and right-click > Paste Layer Style.
3. After scaling the artwork to 200%, use Layer > Layer Style > Scale Effects... and enter 200%.
tools.notes: Save a finished stack as a reusable preset with the New Style button in the Layer Style dialog or the Styles panel (.asl).

tools.name: Blend Modes
tools.description: Determine how a layer's pixels composite with the layers beneath, grouped into darkening (Darken, Multiply, Color Burn, Linear Burn, Darker Color), lightening (Lighten, Screen, Color Dodge, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color), contrast (Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix), comparative (Difference, Exclusion, Subtract, Divide) and component (Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity) families, plus Normal, Dissolve and Pass Through for groups. The contrast family pivots around 50% grey, which is why neutral-grey dodge-and-burn layers work.
tools.usage: Blend mode menu at the top left of the Layers panel, or in the Layer Style dialog. Shift+Plus / Shift+Minus cycles through modes with the Move tool active.

parameters.name: Multiply
parameters.description: Darkens; white becomes transparent. Used for shadows, ink and texture.

parameters.name: Screen
parameters.description: Lightens; black becomes transparent. Used for glows, flares and smoke.

parameters.name: Overlay / Soft Light
parameters.description: Increases contrast around 50% grey - dodge and burn, contrast maps.

parameters.name: Color / Luminosity
parameters.description: Applies only the hue+saturation, or only the brightness, of the layer.

parameters.name: Pass Through
parameters.description: Group-only default: adjustment layers inside reach through to layers below the group.

tools.name: Opacity and Fill
tools.description: Two independent transparency controls. Opacity fades the whole layer including its layer effects; Fill fades only the layer's own pixels and leaves effects at full strength, which is how you get a stroke-only or shadow-only object from a filled shape.
tools.usage: Opacity and Fill fields at the top right of the Layers panel. With the Move tool active, number keys set Opacity (5 = 50%) and Shift+number keys set Fill.

tools.name: Fill layers (Solid Color, Gradient, Pattern)
tools.description: Layers whose content is a live, re-editable colour, gradient or pattern rather than pixels, each created with its own mask. Used for backgrounds, colour washes, gradient maps to the mask, and as a clipped colour source for recolouring artwork; double-click the thumbnail to change the fill at any time.
tools.usage: Layer > New Fill Layer > Solid Color... / Gradient... / Pattern..., or the half-filled circle button at the bottom of the Layers panel.
tools.example:
1. Click the adjustment/fill button in the Layers panel and choose Solid Color.
2. Pick a warm orange and set the layer's blend mode to Soft Light at 25% for a colour grade.
3. Paint black on its mask to exclude the subject.

tools.name: Lock layer (transparency, image, position, artboard, all)
tools.description: Five padlocks at the top of the Layers panel protect parts of a layer: Lock Transparent Pixels confines painting to existing opaque pixels, Lock Image Pixels blocks painting entirely, Lock Position prevents moving, Prevent Auto-Nesting stops the layer hopping between artboards, and Lock All freezes everything.
tools.usage: Lock buttons in the Layers panel. Ctrl+/ toggles Lock All on the selected layers.
tools.example:
1. Select a layer of coloured text pixels.
2. Click Lock Transparent Pixels.
3. Paint freely with a big brush - only the letterforms are recoloured.

JSX: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.transparentPixelsLocked = true;

tools.name: Link Layers
tools.description: Ties selected layers together so they move, transform and scale as a unit while remaining separate layers in the stack. A lighter-weight alternative to grouping when you only need co-ordinated transforms.
tools.usage: Layer > Link Layers, or the chain button at the bottom of the Layers panel. Shift+click a chain icon to disable a link temporarily.
tools.example:
1. Ctrl+click the logo and its shadow layer.
2. Click the chain button.
3. Drag with the Move tool - both travel together.

tools.name: Merge Layers, Merge Visible and Stamp Visible
tools.description: Combines layers into one. Merge Layers (Ctrl+E) merges the selected layers or the layer into the one below, Merge Visible (Shift+Ctrl+E) collapses every visible layer, and the unlisted Stamp Visible shortcut (Shift+Ctrl+Alt+E) creates a new merged copy on top while leaving the originals intact - the standard way to make a flattened layer for sharpening or filtering.
tools.usage: Layer > Merge Layers (Ctrl+E) / Merge Visible (Shift+Ctrl+E); Stamp Visible = Shift+Ctrl+Alt+E.
tools.example:
1. Finish the retouch.
2. Press Shift+Ctrl+Alt+E to stamp a merged copy on top.
3. Convert it to a smart object and apply Smart Sharpen.

JSX: app.activeDocument.mergeVisibleLayers();
tools.notes: Merging is destructive; keep the layered original or work on a duplicate before merging.

tools.name: Flatten Image
tools.description: Collapses every layer into a single Background layer and discards hidden layers, converting transparency to white. Used only as the final step before handing over a flat file, or inside batch scripts to reduce memory before saving a JPEG.
tools.usage: Layer > Flatten Image, or the Layers panel menu.
tools.notes: There is no undo once the file is saved and closed - always keep the layered master.

tools.name: Rasterize
tools.description: Converts vector or live content - type, shape, smart object, fill layer, layer style, 3D or video layer - into ordinary pixels so painting and pixel filters can be used on it. Irreversible loss of editability, so convert to a smart object first when in doubt.
tools.usage: Layer > Rasterize > Type / Shape / Fill Content / Vector Mask / Smart Object / Layer Style / Layer / All Layers, or right-click the layer in the Layers panel.

tools.name: Align and Distribute Layers
tools.description: Lines up two or more selected layers by their left, horizontal centre, right, top, vertical centre or bottom edges, and spreads three or more evenly by edge or by equal spacing. With a selection active, layers align to the selection instead of to each other; inside an artboard they align to the artboard.
tools.usage: Layer > Align / Distribute, or the alignment buttons in the Move tool's options bar (More options offers Distribute Spacing).
tools.example:
1. Ctrl+click the three card layers.
2. Press V and click "Align top edges", then "Distribute horizontal spacing".

JSX: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.link(other); ... then use the align action, or set positions via translate().

tools.name: Auto-Align Layers
tools.description: Analyses overlapping content across selected layers and transforms them so shared detail registers exactly, with Auto, Perspective, Collage, Cylindrical, Spherical and Reposition-only projections plus vignette and geometric distortion correction. Used to stitch panoramas by hand, to align bracketed or hand-held frames before blending, and to combine group photos.
tools.usage: Select two or more layers, then Edit > Auto-Align Layers...

parameters.name: Projection
parameters.description: Auto, Perspective, Collage, Cylindrical, Spherical, Reposition.

parameters.name: Vignette Removal
parameters.description: Evens out corner darkening between frames.

parameters.name: Geometric Distortion
parameters.description: Corrects barrel/pincushion distortion before aligning.

tools.example:
1. File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack, tick "Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images" (or select the layers and run Edit > Auto-Align Layers).
2. Choose Reposition for a tripod-mounted sequence.
3. Follow with Edit > Auto-Blend Layers > Stack Images for a noise-reduced composite.

tools.name: Auto-Blend Layers
tools.description: Blends aligned layers into a seamless result, generating layer masks automatically. Panorama mode feathers overlapping stitched frames; Stack Images picks the best-focused or best-exposed pixels from each layer, which is how focus stacking and crowd removal are done. Seamless Tones and Colors evens out exposure differences between frames.
tools.usage: Select the aligned layers, then Edit > Auto-Blend Layers...

parameters.name: Blend Method
parameters.description: Panorama or Stack Images.

parameters.name: Seamless Tones and Colors
parameters.description: Adjusts colour and exposure so the seams disappear.

parameters.name: Content-Aware Fill Transparent Areas
parameters.description: Fills the ragged edges left by a stitch.

tools.example:
Focus stacking:
1. File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack with auto-align ticked.
2. Select all layers, Edit > Auto-Blend Layers, Blend Method = Stack Images, tick Seamless Tones and Colors.

tools.name: Layer Comps
tools.description: Saved snapshots of the visibility, position and appearance (layer style) of the layers in a document, so several design variants live in one file and can be switched, reviewed and exported. Comps can be exported to files or to a PDF contact sheet, and updated when the design changes.
tools.usage: Window > Layer Comps. Create with the New Layer Comp button; export with File > Export > Layer Comps to Files / Layer Comps to PDF.

parameters.name: Apply To Layer
parameters.description: Which of Visibility, Position and Appearance the comp records.

parameters.name: Comment
parameters.description: Free text shown in the panel and in the exported PDF.

tools.example:
1. Set the layers up for version A and click New Layer Comp, name it "A - blue".
2. Change the colour overlay and create "B - green".

tools.name: Layer filtering and colour labels
tools.description: The filter bar at the top of the Layers panel narrows a long stack by Kind (pixel, adjustment, type, shape, smart object), Name, Effect, Mode, Attribute, Colour label, Smart Object or Selected. Colour labels assigned from the layer context menu give a visual grouping that the filter can then isolate.
tools.usage: Filter menu and the toggle switch at the top of the Layers panel; right-click a layer > choose a colour label.
tools.example:
1. Right-click every retouch layer and label it Red.
2. Set the Layers panel filter to Color > Red to see only those layers.
3. Flip the filter switch off to restore the full stack.
tools.notes: Leaving the filter on is a common source of "my layers disappeared" confusion - the switch at the right end of the filter bar turns it off.
